name: Rollin' Justin
def: Wheeled humanoid from DLR with torque controlled arms and hands, commanded from the International Space Station in orbital telerobotics experiments.
body: Rollin' Justin combines the Justin humanoid upper body, first built in 2006, with a four legged wheeled base whose legs extend and retract, giving 51 degrees of freedom, a height of 1.91 m and a mass around 200 kg. Nearly every joint measures torque, so a hierarchical whole body controller can grip objects softly, absorb collisions and juggle several tasks at once, while the robot carries about 20 kg and moves at up to 2 m/s. In the METERON SUPVIS Justin experiments, astronauts aboard the space station commanded it through a tablet interface to service a mock Mars solar array on the ground in Germany.
facts: Commanded from the International Space Station in the METERON SUPVIS Justin experiments
Torque sensing in nearly every joint for compliant whole body control
Developed at the DLR institute in Wessling, Germany
specs: Torque controlled electric joints with tendon driven hands
Torque sensors in nearly all joints, two stereo cameras, five depth cameras, inertial units
